knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The check-record-escalate step requires stopping the affected task, protecting the area, notifying promptly and recording objective facts. Concealing damage is not allowed.
Access codes and client information are confidential, and only approved communication and storage systems are used.
The lesson says to keep keys and access codes confidential, and to treat access codes, keys, addresses and alarm instructions as confidential.

practicalCriteria: Checks the site/task requirements before acting
Identifies and applies relevant safety and privacy controls
Communicates professionally and respects authorisation boundaries
Records the outcome and escalates unresolved issues correctly
passRule: All safety-critical criteria must be demonstrated; remediate and reassess any missed criterion.
evidenceRequired: Record of procedure step 3: Photograph only where the work order and privacy requirements allow, framing images to avoid personal documents and identifying details.
Record of procedure step 5: Secure the premises when leaving, and report any breakage immediately.
Record of procedure step 7: Notify the designated contact promptly, and record objective facts without concealing damage or attempting unauthorised repair.
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 5 is not done: Secure the premises when leaving, and report any breakage immediately.
Stop work if procedure step 6 is not done: If property is damaged, missing or unexpectedly unsafe, stop the affected task and protect the area.
Stop work if procedure step 8 is not done: Share site details and photographs only through approved systems, never on personal messaging or social media.
